about: How much turning load each friction joint holds, N·mm, as builders measured it by hanging bricks on a lever until the joint gave; written by tools/joint_hold_table.py, read by PoseHold. A kind with no number is not known: it is left unweighed, never guessed.

technic_ball.parts: a 10.2 mm Technic ball in its socket
technic_ball.measured_on: 17114's ball in 92013's socket, the pair 31058-1 uses
technic_ball.how: held 5 2 x 4 bricks on a lever of two 1 x 16 bricks and buckled at 6: the joint lets go between those two loads, levered from the ball's middle, the lever's own weight with them
technic_ball.spread: one joint; friction varies from piece to piece and with wear, new joints holding more [eurobricks-balls]

friction_pin.parts: a pin with friction ridges turning in a round Technic hole (2780, 61332, 4459; the same ridges on 6558, 43093 and their kin)
friction_pin.measured_on: 2780 (10 pins of various ages) and 61332 (8 new pins), one thick liftarm each
friction_pin.how: fell at the count of 2 x 3 bricks in the article's histogram, each pin holding one fewer; both designs together, since a file's 2780 does not say which a builder has
friction_pin.spread: 18 pins; the old design held about a brick more than the new (p = 0.03)

small_ball.parts: a 5.9 mm towball or Mixel ball in its socket (14417, 14418, 14419, 14704, 3184 ...)

click_hinge.parts: a locking hinge's teeth (44301, 44302, 30383, 30364, 30365, 54657 ...), a click rotation joint's (47455 in 48170 or 48171 ...)
click_hinge.why: no measurement published: one builder hung weights on a 32L lever and found the tipping point varied too much to report [bricklink-hinges]

hinge.parts: a friction hinge's pin in its eye (2429 with 2430, 3937 with 3938 ...)

turntable.parts: a turntable's top on its base (3679 with 3680, 61485, 99009 with 99010 ...)

clip.parts: a clip round a bar or a handle

rambling-2017.title: Its new to me: stiffening the joints with Element 74261/6106472 (Element Exposition)
rambling-2017.author: The Rambling Brick
rambling-2017.quote: 2 1×16 bricks are attached to the brick with the ball, and a load is progressively added to the end of the lever. I used standardised 2×4 bricks as my load. [...] The 'naked' ball joint was fairly steady up until the fifth brick was loaded on the lever. When six bricks were loaded onto the lever, the joint rapidly buckled under the load, with virtually no drag.

rambling-2021.title: What if they introduced a new Technic pin, and nobody noticed?
rambling-2021.author: The Rambling Brick
rambling-2021.quote: I inserted it at the proximal hole of an 11 module lift arm, and fashioned a freely rotating weight, consiting of a 5 module long bar, 2 stoppers and 1×2 bricks – 2 with technic hols. The bottom was stabilised using a 2×3 plate. The load was increased, by a 2×3 brick at a time until the arm was unable to resist gravity. [...] A total of 10 'older' and 8 of the newer pins were tested [...] the Older design – 4.5, the newer pin: 3.

eurobricks-balls.title: Question about ball joints (LEGO Action Figures)
eurobricks-balls.author: Eurobricks forum
eurobricks-balls.quote: The friction of a ball joint/ball socket piece usually varies from piece to piece and often depends on how much it was used.

bricklink-hinges.title: Re: Variants Thread - January 26
bricklink-hinges.author: BrickLink forum
bricklink-hinges.quote: hanging some kitchen weights from the end of a Technic brick attached to another one attached to the hinge, so 32L long [...] Either there is huge variability between hinges or variability comes through the connections between all the parts.
